metadata.title: A categorical equivalence between affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras and some quiver Hecke algebras

extraction_notes.note: The proof of Theorem 2.10 is prose split by unnumbered \subsubsection* case headings, which count as section boundaries; it is emitted as one proof node per section part, each proving TP2 and using the first part PP8. Some parts also hold text that logically opens the next block (e.g. PP15 starts with the last line of a case and then begins the Psi-verification).
Consecutive case headings (Cases 2-4, Cases 1-3) have no text between them, so the empty sections get no node and the shared argument sits under the last heading.

The text says 'the braid relations (2.2)' but (2.2) is a quiver Hecke relation; the intended relation is the Yokonuma-Hecke braid relation rel-def-Y2 (in EP9), linked by hand. The label M-J is also defined twice (EP15 and EP34).

These numbered identities are introduced by a justifying clause in the same sentence ('By (2.4), we get the following useful identity:'); they are kept as equation nodes with hand-added uses edges, and the Demazure operator definition after EP3 stays unnoded inside that sentence.
claim or definition: the sentences assert existence of the weight idempotents e(nu,j) and simultaneously introduce the symbol; kept as claims.

Historical survey results in the Introduction (Kazhdan-Lusztig, Ariki, Brundan-Kleshchev, Rostam, etc.) are not extracted except Rouquier's equivalence, which the main theorems generalize; results of [BK]/[BK1] applied inside proofs are not separate nodes.

nodes.name: Rouquier's categorical equivalence theorem
nodes.statement: Rouquier \cite{Rou1} also proved that certain module category of an affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebra is equivalent to its suitable counterpart of some quiver Hecke algebra of (affine) type $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Module categories of affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebras are equivalent to suitable module categories of quiver Hecke algebras of (affine) type A.
conclusions: certain module category of an affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebra is equivalent to its suitable counterpart of some quiver Hecke algebra of (affine) type $A$

nodes.name: Base field $k$ with primitive $r$th root of unity $\zeta$
nodes.statement: Let $r, n\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1},$ and let $k$ be a field which contains a primitive $r$th root of unity $\zeta.$
differentia: contains a primitive $r$th root of unity $\zeta.$

nodes.name: Characteristic $p$ and parameter $q$
nodes.statement: Let $p$ be the characteristic of $k$ and consider an element $q\in k^{*}.$

nodes.name: Quantum characteristic $e$
nodes.statement: We denote by $e$ the smallest integer such that $1+q+\cdots+q^{e-1}=0$, and set $e:=\infty$ if no such integer exists.
nodes.statement_short: $e$ is the least integer with $1+q+\cdots+q^{e-1}=0$, or $\infty$.

nodes.name: Quiver $I_{1}$
nodes.statement: Assume first that $q=1.$ Given a subset $I$ of $k,$ we denote by $I_{1}$ the quiver with set of vertices $I$ and with an arrow $i\rightarrow i+1$ whenever $i, i+1\in I.$
differentia: with set of vertices $I$ and with an arrow $i\rightarrow i+1$ whenever $i, i+1\in I.$

nodes.name: Quiver $I_{q}$
nodes.statement: Assume now that $q\neq 1.$ Given a subset $I$ of $k^{*},$ we denote by $I_{q}$ the quiver with set of vertices $I$ and with an arrow $i\rightarrow qi$ whenever $i, qi\in I.$
differentia: with set of vertices $I$ and with an arrow $i\rightarrow qi$ whenever $i, qi\in I.$

nodes.name: Connectedness of $I_{q}$
nodes.statement: Assume that $I_{q}$ is connected.

nodes.name: Types of the quiver $I_{q}$
nodes.statement: Note that when $q=1,$ $I_{q}$ has type $A_{\ell}$ if $\vert I\vert=\ell< p$ or $|I|=\ell$ and $p=0;$ type $A_{\infty}$ if $|I|=\infty$ and $p=0;$ type $\widetilde{A}_{p-1}$ if $|I|=p> 0.$ When $q\neq 1,$ $I_{q}$ has type $A_{\ell}$ if $\vert I\vert=\ell< e$ or $|I|=\ell$ and $e=\infty;$ type $A_{\infty}$ if $|I|=\infty$ and $e=\infty;$ type $\widetilde{A}_{e-1}$ if $|I|=e> 0.$
nodes.statement_short: $I_q$ is of type $A_\ell$, $A_\infty$ or affine $\widetilde{A}$ depending on $|I|$ and on $p$ (if $q=1$) or $e$ (if $q\neq1$).

nodes.name: Quiver $\Gamma$ ($r$ disjoint copies of $I_q$)
nodes.statement: We now define the quiver $\Gamma=\coprod_{j\in J} I_{q},$ which is $r$ disjoint copies of $I_{q}.$

nodes.name: Vertex set $K=I\times J$ of $\Gamma$
nodes.statement: Hence, the vertices of $\Gamma$ are the elements of $K=I\times J$ and there is an arrow between $(i, j)$ and $(i', j')$ in $\Gamma$ if and only if there is an arrow between $i$ and $i'$ in $I_{q}$ and $j=j'.$
nodes.statement_short: Vertices of $\Gamma$ are $K=I\times J$; arrows only between copies with equal $j$.

nodes.name: Double arrow $k\rightleftarrows k'$
nodes.statement: For $k, k'\in K,$ we write $k\rightleftarrows k'$ whenever $k\rightarrow k'$ and $k'\rightarrow k$; this happens only when $e=2.$

nodes.name: Non-adjacent vertices $k\:\notslash\: k'$
nodes.statement: Finally, we write $k\:\notslash\: k'$ if $k\neq k'$ and if there is no arrow between these two vertices.

nodes.name: Ground ring $\mathcal{R}$
nodes.statement: Let $q$ be an indeterminate and let $\mathcal{R}=\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1}{r}][q,q^{-1}].$ We consider $k$ as an $\mathcal{R}$-algebra by mapping $q$ to the invertible element $q\in k^{*}.$

nodes.name: Affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebra $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(q)$
nodes.statement: The affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebra, denoted by $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(q)$, is an $\mathcal{R}$-associative algebra generated by the elements $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},g_{1},\ldots,g_{n-1},X_{1}^{\pm1},$ in which the generators $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},g_{1},$ $\ldots,g_{n-1}$ satisfy the following relations: \begin{align} g_ig_j&=g_jg_i \qquad \qquad\qquad\quad\hspace{0.3cm}\mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n-1$ such that $\vert i-j\vert \geq 2$;} \\[0.1em] g_ig_{i+1}g_i&=g_{i+1}g_ig_{i+1} \qquad \quad\qquad\hspace{0.05cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-2$;} \\[0.1em] t_it_j&=t_jt_i \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad \mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.1em] g_it_j&=t_{s_i(j)}g_i \quad \quad\qquad\qquad\hspace{0.25cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$ and $j=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.1em] t_i^r&=1 \quad \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.2em] g_{i}^{2}&=q+(q-1)e_{i}g_{i} \qquad \hspace{0.48cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$;} \end{align} where $s_{i}$ is the transposition $(i,i+1)$, and for each $1\leq i\leq n-1$, $$e_{i} :=\frac{1}{r}\sum\limits_{s=0}^{r-1}t_{i}^{s}t_{i+1}^{-s},$$ together with the following relations concerning the generators $X_{1}^{\pm1}$: \begin{align} X_{1}X_{1}^{-1}&=X_{1}^{-1}X_{1}=1; \\[0.1em] g_{1}X_{1}g_{1}X_{1}&=X_{1}g_{1}X_{1}g_{1}; \\[0.1em] g_{i}X_{1}&=X_{1}g_{i} \qquad \qquad \quad\mbox{for all $i=2,\ldots,n-1$;} \\[0.1em] t_{j}X_{1}&=X_{1}t_{j} \qquad \qquad\quad\mbox{for all $j=1,\ldots,n$;} \end{align}

u, j)\in K^{n},$ which can be proved by discussing the following five cases:\vspace{0.2cm} Case 1: $j_i=j_{i+1}=j_{i+2};$ Case 2: $j_i=j_{i+1}
eq j_{i+2};$ Case 3: $j_i
eq j_{i+1}=j_{i+2};$ Case 4: $j_i=j_{i+2}
eq j_{i+1};$ Case 5: $j_i, j_{i+1}, j_{i+2}$ are all different.\vspace{0.2cm} By $e_{i}e(
u, j)=e_{i+1}e(
u, j)=e(
u, j),$ Case 1 comes down to the case of affine Hecke algebra of type $A,$ which is exactly [BK, (4.13)]. For Case 2, after a careful calculation, we get that  egin{align*}\Theta_{i}\Theta_{i+1}\Theta_{i}e(
u, j)=&g_{i}g_{i+1}g_{i}(1-X_{i+1}X_{i+2}^{-1})(1-X_{i}X_{i+2}^{-1})(1-X_{i}X_{i+1}^{-1})e(
u, j)\&+(1-q)g_{i}(1-X_{i}X_{i+1}^{-1})g_{i+1}(1-X_{i+1}X_{i+2}^{-1})e(
u, j),\end{align*} and  egin{align*}\Theta_{i+1}\Theta_{i}\Theta_{i+1}e(

u, j)\&+(1-q)g_{i}(1-X_{i}X_{i+1}^{-1})g_{i+1}(1-X_{i+1}X_{i+2}^{-1})e(
u, j).\end{align*} Thus, Case 2 holds by the braid relation \eqref{rel-def-Y2}. Case 3 holds similarly. For Case 4, after a careful calculation, we get that  egin{align*}\Theta_{i}\Theta_{i+1}\Theta_{i}e(
u, j)=&g_{i}g_{i+1}g_{i}(1-X_{i+1}X_{i+2}^{-1})(1-X_{i}X_{i+2}^{-1})(1-X_{i}X_{i+1}^{-1})e(
u, j)\&+(1-q)g_{i}^{2}(1-X_{i+1}X_{i+2}^{-1})(1-X_{i}X_{i+1}^{-1})e(
u, j),\end{align*} and  egin{align*}\Theta_{i+1}\Theta_{i}\Theta_{i+1}e(
u, j)=&g_{i+1}g_{i}g_{i+1}(1-X_{i}X_{i+1}^{-1})(1-X_{i}X_{i+2}^{-1})(1-X_{i+1}X_{i+2}^{-1})e(
u, j)\&+(1-q)g_{i+1}^{2}(1-X_{i}X_{i+1}^{-1})(1-X_{i+1}X_{i+2}^{-1})e(
u, j).\end{align*} Thus, Case 4 holds by the braid relation \eqref{rel-def-Y2} and the fact that $g_{i}^{2}e(
u, j)=g_{i+1}^{2}e(
u, j)=qe(
u, j)$. For Case 5, after a careful calculation, we get that  egin{align*}\Theta_{i}\Theta_{i+1}\Theta_{i}e(
u, j)=g_{i}g_{i+1}g_{i}(1-X_{i+1}X_{i+2}^{-1})(1-X_{i}X_{i+2}^{-1})(1-X_{i}X_{i+1}^{-1})e(
u, j),\end{align*} and  egin{align*}\Theta_{i+1}\Theta_{i}\Theta_{i+1}e(
u, j)=g_{i+1}g_{i}g_{i+1}(1-X_{i}X_{i+1}^{-1})(1-X_{i}X_{i+2}^{-1})(1-X_{i+1}X_{i+2}^{-1})e(
u, j).\end{align*} Thus, Case 5 holds by the braid relation \eqref{rel-def-Y2}. We now prove \eqref{phie-ephi}. If $j_{i}=j_{i+1},$ the identity follows from [BK, (4.14)]; if $j_{i}
eq j_{i+1},$ the identity follows from \eqref{ge-eg}.

nodes.statement: The degenerate affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebra, denoted by $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(1)$, is an $\mathcal{R}$-associative algebra generated by the elements $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},f_{1},\ldots,f_{n-1},y_1,\ldots, y_{n}$ in which the generators $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},g_{1},$ $\ldots,g_{n-1}$ satisfy the following relations: \begin{align} f_if_j&=f_jf_i \qquad \qquad\qquad\quad\hspace{0.3cm}\mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n-1$ such that $\vert i-j\vert \geq 2$;} \\[0.1em] f_if_{i+1}f_i&=f_{i+1}f_if_{i+1} \qquad \quad\qquad\hspace{0.05cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-2$;} \\[0.1em] t_it_j&=t_jt_i \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad \mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.1em] f_it_j&=t_{s_i(j)}f_i \quad \quad\qquad\qquad\hspace{0.25cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$ and $j=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.1em] t_i^r&=1 \quad \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.2em] f_{i}^{2}&=1 \qquad \hspace{2.71cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$;} \end{align} together with the following relations concerning the generators $y_1,\ldots, y_{n}$: \begin{align} y_{i}y_{j}&=y_{j}y_{i}; \\[0.1em] f_{i}y_{i+1}&=y_{i}f_{i}+e_{i}; \\[0.1em] f_{i}y_{j}&=y_{j}f_{i} \qquad \qquad \quad\mbox{for all $j\neq i, i+1$;} \\[0.1em] t_{j}y_{i}&=y_{i}t_{j} \hspace{0.07cm}\qquad \qquad\quad\mbox{for all $i, j=1,\ldots,n$;} \end{align} where for each $1\leq i\leq n-1$, $$e_{i} :=\frac{1}{r}\sum\limits_{s=0}^{r-1}t_{i}^{s}t_{i+1}^{-s}.$$
